questions.prompt: Explain the concept of faulting in Core Data and why it helps performance. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that faulting lazily loads object attributes as hollow placeholders without loading full data upfront
Explains that faulting saves memory and improves query speed by reading disk data only when properties are accessed

questions.modelAnswer: Faulting is Core Data lazy loading mechanism where queried objects load into memory as hollow placeholder records. The actual attribute and relationship data remains on disk until your code explicitly reads a property. This prevents large object graphs from consuming unnecessary RAM and accelerates initial fetch speeds.

questions.prompt: Explain what NSPersistentContainer does in a Core Data stack. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that NSPersistentContainer encapsulates the managed object model, persistent store coordinator, and managed object context
Mentions that it simplifies stack setup and provides viewContext for UI and background context creation

questions.modelAnswer: NSPersistentContainer simplifies Core Data setup by managing the managed object model, store coordinator, and contexts in one place. It exposes the main-thread viewContext for user interface rendering. It also provides helper methods like newBackgroundContext() and performBackgroundTask for asynchronous data processing.

questions.prompt: Why are NSManagedObject and NSManagedObjectContext not thread-safe, and how do you access them correctly? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that managed objects and contexts are strictly bound to the specific queue or thread where they were created
Explains that developers must execute work inside perform or performAndWait, and pass NSManagedObjectID across threads

questions.modelAnswer: Core Data managed objects and contexts are confined to their specific dispatch queues. Interacting with them from other threads causes race conditions, corrupted object state, and crashes. Developers must wrap all context operations inside perform or performAndWait, and pass thread-safe NSManagedObjectID tokens between contexts.

questions.prompt: How do you propagate changes saved in a background context to the main viewContext? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains setting automaticallyMergesChangesFromParent to true on viewContext
Explains that background context saves commit to the store coordinator, which then automatically updates viewContext

questions.modelAnswer: To synchronize changes, configure viewContext by setting automaticallyMergesChangesFromParent to true. When a background context commits updates to the persistent store coordinator, the coordinator notifies the main context. The main context merges these changes into memory automatically so the UI reflects updated data.

questions.prompt: What causes the N+1 fault firing problem in Core Data and how do you resolve it? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that accessing unloaded relationships inside a loop fires individual database queries for each object
Explains resolving it using relationshipKeyPathsForPrefetching on the fetch request to batch load related data

questions.modelAnswer: The N+1 problem occurs when iterating through an array of objects and accessing an unloaded relationship on each item. Because relationships are faults, Core Data executes a separate disk query for every single iteration. To solve this, specify relationshipKeyPathsForPrefetching on the NSFetchRequest so related entities load together in a batch.
